articles.title_original: Seven Ethiopian rebel groups form new alliance
articles.title_zh: Seven Ethiopian rebel groups form new alliance
facts_zh:
Seven Ethiopian rebel groups form new alliance
- Published
Several of the rebel groups which have been fighting the Ethiopian authorities in different parts of the country have announced they have formed an alliance to remove the government in Addis Ababa.

The alliance brings together the Fano militia in Amhara, the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA), Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and four other smaller groupings in a coalition named Alliance for Survival.
The seven groups accuse Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government of presiding over "war, genocide, mass destruction and utter poverty", claiming Ethiopia is at risk of disintegration.

all_titles.en: Seven Ethiopian rebel groups form new alliance

articles.title_original: First UK charges brought over 1994 Rwanda genocide
articles.title_zh: First UK charges brought over 1994 Rwanda genocide
facts_zh:
First UK charges brought over 1994 Rwanda genocide
- Published
A Rwandan man, who has been living in north London, has become the first person charged in the UK with offences relating to the 1994 Rwanda genocide against the Tutsi, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) has said.
Dr Vincent Brown, formerly Dr Vincent Bajinya, 65, has been charged with one offence of conduct ancillary to genocide and six offences of conduct ancillary to murder as a crime against humanity.
Frank Ferguson, head of the CPS's Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division, said Brown "is alleged to have directed and incited acts of murder and genocide carried out by others".

all_titles.en: First UK charges brought over 1994 Rwanda genocide

articles.title_zh: Merz vows to keep coalition together for Germany's 'democratic future'
facts_zh:
Merz vows to keep coalition together for Germany's 'democratic future'
- Published
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz says he will keep his ruling coalition together for the sake of his country's "democratic future", following resounding defeats for his party in two state elections.

"We are determined to live up to the historic challenges our country is facing," Merz said, referring to the coalition between his Christian Democratic Unionist (CDU) party and the Social Democratic Party (SPD).
Merz's position has come under mounting pressure after Sunday's election results.

articles.title_zh: Yemenis flee across Red Sea as Houthis and Saudi-backed forces escalate war
facts_zh:
Yemenis flee across Red Sea as Houthis and Saudi-backed forces escalate war
- Published
Ibrahim Issa, 50, is from the Yemeni coastal town of Dhubab, right on the front lines of the war between Yemen's Houthis and the Saudi-backed pro-government forces fighting them.

Today he sits, surrounded by his family, on a tarpaulin spread over a sandy floor inside a vast open-sided warehouse at Markazi camp in Obock, northern Djibouti, packed with Yemeni families who have fled by boat across the narrow Bab al-Mandab Strait.
After their sea crossing, Yemeni refugees have made their way by truck and on foot to this camp, jointly administered by the government and the UN.

articles.title_zh: Google hit with €403m fine by Irish data watchdog over GDPR violations
facts_zh:
Google hit with €403m fine by Irish data watchdog over GDPR violations
- Published
Google has been fined €403m (£345m) by the Republic of Ireland's Data Protection Commission (DPC) over its handling of location data.

The penalty - one of the largest of its kind imposed by the Irish watchdog authority - followed an inquiry launched into the tech giant six years ago, following complaints from several European consumer rights organisations.
On Monday the DPC said its investigation found Google had processed data in a manner that was not "lawful", "fair" or "transparent".

all_titles.en: Google hit with €403m fine by Irish data watchdog over GDPR violations

articles.title_original: Three held over woman's murder as South Africa police investigate eight other body finds
articles.title_zh: Three held over woman's murder as South Africa police investigate eight other body finds
facts_zh:
Three held over woman's murder as South Africa police investigate eight other body finds
- Published
Three suspects have been detained in South Africa in connection with the murder of a woman in an area east of Johannesburg – the last of nine recent cases in that region that has shone a spotlight on the level of violence against women in the country.
Under pressure to solve the spate of murders which has involved victims' bodies being dumped on a roadside, police have described the arrests of the three – a man and two women - as a "breakthrough".
Referring to all nine cases, acting police chief Lt Gen Puleng Dimpane said her officers were "working tirelessly to bring those responsible to justice".

all_titles.en: Three held over woman's murder as South Africa police investigate eight other body finds

articles.title_original: US and China discuss AI safety plan ahead of Trump-Xi summit
articles.title_zh: US and China discuss AI safety plan ahead of Trump-Xi summit
facts_zh:
US and China discuss AI safety plan ahead of Trump-Xi summit
- Published
Top US and Chinese officials have discussed creating a new "notification mechanism" for AI incidents that could affect national security, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told reporters on Sunday.
Bessent made the comments after what he called "successful" talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York.
The meeting came as US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are due to hold a summit in Washington later this week.

all_titles.en: US and China discuss AI safety plan ahead of Trump-Xi summit
